# filmopen_engine_bench

*Generated by `scripts/package_digest.py`; regenerate, never edit.*

The timeline engines' bench (Software Specification §19.11): a Flutter app for Linux and Windows that drives any `TimelineEngine`, wrapped in `LoggingEngine`, through the fixture scene of `scripts/make_timeline_fixture.py` and writes `bench-report.json` and `bench-report.md` — each measure's n, p50, p95 and max, its gate and **pass**, **fail** or **not measured**.

**Flutter.** 4 files, 1,115 lines under `lib/`; 29 tests in 4 files. Barrel: `lib/filmopen_engine_bench.dart`.

## Depends on

- **filmopen_engine** — uses `EngineClock`, `EngineException`, `EngineItem`, `EnginePresented`, `EngineSubtitle`, `EngineTimeline`, `EngineTrack`, `ExportSettings`, `FakeEngine`, `LoggingEngine`, `MediaProbe`, `TimelineEngine`, `frameAt`, `frameStart`
- **filmopen_engine_mlt** — uses `MltEngine`, `MltTexture`
- **filmopen_engine_mpv** — uses `MpvEngine`
- **filmopen_store** — uses `AppLog`, `LogLevel`, `MemoryLogSink`, `openFileLogSink`

## Used by

No package of FilmOpen.

## Public API

What the barrel exports, file by file. A name is `class`, `enum`, `mixin`, `extension`, `typedef`, a top-level function, getter, setter or variable; under a class, its public constructors, fields, getters, setters and methods.

### `lib/bench.dart`

- **getter** `String get benchLockPath` — The one lock of the bench and the builds: the OS byte-range lock on this file (`scripts/with_bench_lock.py`); `FILMOPEN_BENCH_LOCK` names another, which only the tests do.
- **function** `Future<RandomAccessFile?> takeBenchLock({String? path, void Function(String? pid)? holder})` — Takes the bench lock at [path] without waiting; null, with the holder's pid in [holder], when another process holds it.
- **class `BenchConfig`** — What a run is given: the engine's name, the fixture's media folder, the manifests, where the reports go.
  - `const BenchConfig({ required this.engine, required this.fixtureDir, required this.repoRoot, required this.outDir, this.seed = 714, this.playMinutes…` — A run's configuration; the seed defaults to 714 and the sustained play to ten minutes.
  - `final String engine, fixtureDir, repoRoot, outDir` — The engine's name, the media folder, the repository root and the report folder.
  - `final int seed, playMinutes` — The seed of the exact seeks, and the minutes of the sustained play.
  - `final String? baselineDir` — The release bundle of this bench without any engine plug-in, which the engine's size is counted against.
  - `final String? subtitlesFile` — A JSON file of subtitles laid over the scene (`withSubtitles`), for measuring it with and without the overlay.
  - `final String? fontsDir` — The fonts folder an engine hands libass: the repository's `assets/fonts` unless named (the bench's own bundle holds none).
  - `String get fonts` — The fonts folder in use.
  - `String get manifest` — The scene's manifest.
  - `String get stress` — The stress set's manifest.
  - `String get verifyScript` — The fixture script, whose `verify` checks an export.
- **function** `Map<String, Object?> withSubtitles(Map<String, Object?> manifest, Map<String, Object?> subtitles)` — [manifest] with the subtitles of [subtitles] — an object of `subtitles`, `subtitle_font` and `subtitle_size`, as an `EngineTimeline`'s JSON has them, and nothing else (a [FormatException] otherwise) — so the scene is…
- **class `Measure`** — One line of the report.
  - `Measure(this.name, {this.stats, this.value, required this.gate, required this.result, this.note})` — A measure named [name] against its [gate].
  - `final String name` — What was measured.
  - `final Stats? stats` — Its distribution, where it has one.
  - `final Object? value` — Its single value, where it has one.
  - `final String gate` — The gate it is judged by.
  - `final String result` — `pass`, `fail` or `not measured`.
  - `final String? note` — Why a result is what it is, where that is not plain.
  - `Map<String, Object?> toJson()` — The measure as the report's JSON.
- **class `Bench`** — Runs the bench once; [capture] reads the code of the picture on screen, or is null where nothing can be read.
  - `Bench(this.config, this.makeEngine, {required this.log, this.capture, this.onStage})` — A bench of [config] that builds its engines with [makeEngine].
  - `final BenchConfig config` — What the run is given.
  - `final TimelineEngine Function() makeEngine` — Builds a new engine; each stage takes its own.
  - `final AppLog log` — Where every line of the run goes.
  - `final Future<(int, int)?> Function()? capture` — Reads the code of the picture on screen; null, or a null answer, where nothing can be read.
  - `final void Function(String stage, TimelineEngine? engine)? onStage` — Told each stage and the engine it runs, so the window can show it.
  - `final measures` — The measures so far, in the run's order.
  - `Future<int> run()` — The whole run; the exit code is 0 when it ran to the end (pass or fail is the report's), 1 when refused or failed.
  - `Future<void> stress()` — The stress set: each file its own timeline, a refusal checked by its code, a play case played and observed (Software Specification §19.11).
  - `Future<void> cancelAtHalf(TimelineEngine engine, EngineTimeline timeline)` — One export of [timeline] cancelled once its progress reaches half way; *not measured* when it never did, since a job that ended or never got there proves nothing about cancelling one in flight.
  - `Future<void> cycles(EngineTimeline timeline, {int count = 50})` — [count] cycles of prepare, play, twenty scrubs, replace, seek, export and dispose: no crash, no record of an older revision from the replace on, no process and no file left (Software Specification §19.11).
- **function** `(int, int) expectedCode(Map<String, Object?> manifest, int n)` — The (clip id, source frame) the manifest says timeline frame [n] shows, as `make_timeline_fixture.py` computes it.
- **function** `EngineTimeline repeated(EngineTimeline t, Duration atLeast)` — [t]'s items and subtitles repeated along a timeline at least [atLeast] long, one revision on: the 10-minute play is one timeline, never the player restarted.

### `lib/measures.dart`

- **class `Stats`** — The n, p50, p95 and max of a list of milliseconds; nearest-rank percentiles.
  - `const Stats(this.n, this.p50, this.p95, this.max)` — Stats of [n] values.
  - `final int n` — How many values.
  - `final double p50, p95, max` — The median, the 95th percentile and the largest, in milliseconds.
  - `factory Stats.of(Iterable<double> values)` — The stats of [values]; all zero when there are none.
  - `Map<String, Object?> toJson()` — The stats as the report's JSON, rounded to 0.01.
- **function** `double? firstFrameMs(int fromUs, Iterable<EnginePresented> records)` — Milliseconds from [fromUs] to the first record presented at or after it; null when none was.
- **function** `List<double> requestLatenciesMs(Map<int, int> requestUs, Iterable<EnginePresented> records)` — Each answered request's latency (ms): from its stamp in [requestUs] to the first record whose `request` is it.
- **function** `double longestGapMs(Iterable<int> instantsUs, {int? startUs, int? endUs})` — The longest interval (ms) between consecutive instants of [instantsUs] in order, from [startUs] to [endUs]: the longest stretch with no new frame on screen.
- **function** `({int shouldShow, int onTime}) onTime(List<EnginePresented> play, int fpsNum, int fpsDen, int firstFrame, int lastFrame)` — How many frames of a play were on time, of those the timeline should have shown.
- **function** `List<double> avOffsetsMs(Iterable<EnginePresented> records, int fpsNum, int fpsDen)` — The software A/V offset (ms) of each record that carries the audio clock: `audioUs − frameStart(frame)`.
- **function** `(int, int)? readCode(List<int> rgba, int width, {required double left, required double top, required double square})` — The (clip id, frame) a 16-square code shows, read from RGBA pixels: [square] px squares along the top of the picture whose top-left corner is at ([left], [top]) in an image [width] px wide.
